findings_addressed: FIX-6 [P2] 1/1 — ORIGINLESS DIRECT COMPONENTS BYPASSED THE TIER ORACLE (scripts/sbom-survey/tests/test_cyclonedx.py, AC-SBOM-11). Authorized as a bounded round by Steward ruling seq-162: one finding, no sweep. The criterion's VALUE leg iterated the emitted components and did `if len(origins) != 1: continue`, which was written for the multi-origin case (a package declared by two manifests of different tiers has no single ruled answer) but SILENTLY SWALLOWED THE ZERO-ORIGIN CASE TOO. That is a hole with a specific exploit: a Slice-32 run_survey() could read an UNTRACKED / GITIGNORED manifest — python/pyproject.toml is the exact case REQ/AC-SBOM-02 exists to prevent — emit those dependencies WITH NO fathomdb:declared-in origin, and pass BOTH this tier oracle AND the discovery-boundary checks added at fix-4, because those checks can only constrain the origins that are actually PRESENT ('every origin must be a path git ls-files reports' says nothing about a component that carries no origin at all). The vacuity guard did not catch it either: one other component carrying an origin satisfies `assert graded`. So an entire untracked dependency tree could reach the BOM ungraded, untiered-in-effect, and invisible to the very criteria written to keep the survey inside `git ls-files`. CLOSED by splitting the zero-origin case out and ASSERTING it rather than skipping: a component tagged fathomdb:depth == 'direct' with NO origin FAILS, with a message that names the untracked-manifest-leakage class it guards, cites §5.5 and points at AC-SBOM-02. The grounding is definitional rather than invented: §5.5 already defines depth = 'direct' IFF the package name appears in a dependency table of at least one TRACKED, NON-EXCLUDED manifest, so a direct component with no declaring manifest CONTRADICTS THE SPEC — this fix does not add an obligation to Slice 32, it stops the suite from tolerating a violation of one §5.5 already stated.

FIX-6 — HOW THE LEGITIMATE ORIGINLESS CASE WAS KEPT PASSING, which is the whole care of this fix. Lockfile-only TRANSITIVES have no declaring manifest BY CONSTRUCTION (§5.5): they exist only because a lockfile-derived library<->library edge put them there, and the five pinned crates AC-SBOM-12 requires to arrive tagged `transitive` (proc-macro2, quote, syn, unicode-ident, serde_derive) are exactly that population. A blanket 'every component must carry an origin' would have made AC-SBOM-11 and AC-SBOM-12 MUTUALLY UNSATISFIABLE — AC-SBOM-12 demands those crates be present, AC-SBOM-11 would have forbidden them — so Slice 32 could not have turned the suite green at all. The assertion is therefore CONDITIONED on depth == 'direct' and reads `assert depth != "direct"`, so zero-origin `transitive` components remain exempt and the failure message says so explicitly ('Transitive components with no origin are legitimate (§5.5) and remain exempt'). The MULTI-ORIGIN skip is also untouched: `if len(origins) != 1: continue` still follows, so a package declared by two manifests of different tiers still has its VALUE ungraded, exactly as fix-4 ruled. The depth is read with a `next(..., None)` default rather than an index, so the new branch cannot itself raise on a malformed component — AC-SBOM-12 is the criterion that owns 'every component carries exactly one fathomdb:depth in {direct, transitive}', and duplicating that grade here would have been the sweep this round was forbidden.

FIX-5 [P2] (round 5, STILL CLOSED) — OVER-SPECIFIC CLI ORACLE FOR THE UNTIERED-MANIFEST ERROR (scripts/sbom-survey/tests/test_cli.py, AC-SBOM-21). THIS FINDING IS THE INVERSE OF THE CLASS THE PREVIOUS FOUR ROUNDS FIXED. Every one of the ten earlier findings was a test too PERMISSIVE — it would let a wrong implementation pass. This one is too STRICT: it would REJECT A CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION. The criterion drives the CLI with a tier map whose single rule excludes dev/release/fixtures/ and therefore covers NO real manifest, and REQ-4 then requires only that the CLI NAME THE OFFENDING PATH on stderr. The assertion was `assert "Cargo.toml" in proc.stderr`, which accepts exactly one basename. A Slice-32 implementation that walks discovered paths in `git ls-files` order legitimately fails FIRST on Cargo.lock — or on any other tracked manifest, since the order in which the tool reaches an untiered path is an implementation choice REQ-4 does not constrain — names that path, satisfies REQ-4 in full, and STILL FAILS THIS TEST. CLOSED by asserting that stderr names SOME MEMBER OF THE SET of currently-untiered tracked manifests: the 21 tracked manifest paths that lie outside dev/release/fixtures/ (29 tracked manifests minus the 8 skew fixtures the one rule excludes), DERIVED FROM GIT through the suite's existing conftest.tracked_manifest_paths() helper rather than written as a second literal list — a hand-maintained list is exactly what drifted in rounds 1-3 (the missing setup.cfg, the stale 28). A VACUITY GUARD fails the criterion if that set is ever empty, since a tier map that happened to cover the whole repository would leave the assertion grading nothing. The failure message prints the full expected set alongside the actual stderr, so a Slice-32 implementer sees immediately what would have satisfied it.

FIX-5 (round 5, STILL CLOSED) — AC-SBOM-07 CHECKED FOR THE SAME DEFECT AND DOES NOT HAVE IT. The round-5 steer asked whether the sibling unit-level criterion (test_tiering.py::test_untiered_manifest_raises_untiered_manifest_error, which asserts UntieredManifestError names the path) carries the same over-specificity. It does not, and the reason is structural rather than incidental: TierMap.classify() is handed EXACTLY ONE path by the test ('some/brand/new/Cargo.toml'), so the error it raises can only be about THAT path — there is no discovery order, no set of candidates and no choice of victim, which means naming it is the SOLE correct behaviour and asserting it rejects nothing correct. The over-specificity is only possible where THE TOOL PICKS THE PATH ITSELF, which in this suite is the CLI alone. No change was made to AC-SBOM-07, and design §5.3 now states the distinction so it is not re-litigated.

FIX-4 [P2] 1/2 (round 4, STILL CLOSED) — THE INJECTED PUBLISHED-SOURCE WAS NEVER EXERCISED THROUGH run_survey (test_registry.py, AC-SBOM-17). The criterion called classify_status() DIRECTLY, so Slice 32 could ship a correct comparator while run_survey(..., published=...) never called published.latest() and left every staleness row 'unknown' — and AC-SBOM-15/16 would still pass, because both inject a source that legitimately yields 'unknown' for everything. CLOSED by a second leg that drives a POSITIVE StaticSource THROUGH run_survey and asserts on the resulting staleness rows: 'current', 'outdated' and 'ahead' must all appear, each carrying the INJECTED latest_version, while every package absent from the mapping stays 'unknown' / None (which is what stops a blanket fill). Probes are taken from a preceding offline run rather than hardcoded, and constrained to a unique (ecosystem, name) and a plain major.minor.patch with major >= 1 so both sentinels (9999.0.0, 0.0.1) order unambiguously under BOTH comparators. Design §5.4 carries the probe table.
